sections.title: Introduction and Greeting
observations: Paul introduces himself as an apostle, emphasizing that his authority comes not from men but from Jesus Christ and God the Father. This establishes the divine authority behind his message.
The greeting includes a blessing of grace and peace, which is a common Pauline greeting, but it also sets the tone for the themes of grace that will be explored throughout the letter.

sections.title: The Distortion of the Gospel
observations: Paul expresses astonishment that the Galatians are turning to a different gospel, which is not really another gospel at all. This highlights the seriousness of the issue at hand.
He emphasizes that any person or angel who preaches a different gospel should be accursed, underscoring the importance of adhering to the true gospel of Christ.
This section serves as a warning against false teachings and the necessity of maintaining the purity of the gospel message.

sections.title: Paul's Defense of His Apostolic Authority
observations: Paul recounts his past as a zealous persecutor of the church, which serves to illustrate the radical transformation he underwent after encountering Christ.
He emphasizes that his revelation of the gospel came directly from Jesus Christ, not from human sources, reinforcing his authority as an apostle.
This personal testimony serves to validate his message and to remind the Galatians of the divine origin of the gospel they received.

importantVerses.commentary: I am astonished that you are so quickly deserting the one who called you to live in the grace of Christ and are turning to a different gospel.
But even if we or an angel from heaven should preach a gospel other than the one we preached to you, let them be under God’s curse!

questions: What does it mean to turn to a different gospel, and how can we identify false teachings today?
How does Paul's authority as an apostle impact the way we understand his teachings?
In what ways does Paul's personal testimony serve as a model for our own understanding of grace and transformation?
